breaking.headline: Nasdaq slides into correction as stocks close sharply lower
breaking.fact: The S&P 500 fell 1.92% to 7,416.59, the Nasdaq 2.49% to 24,509.76 — now more than 10% below its Oct 6 high, a correction — and the Dow 739 points to 51,608.17, a third straight down day; Nvidia fell 4.12% to $156.14 ahead of Tuesday’s earnings and the VIX jumped to 22.91.

breaking.headline: Nvidia board rules out Huang comeback as petition tops 180,000
breaking.fact: Nvidia’s board is not weighing a return for Jensen Huang as CEO, three people told Reuters, despite a “Stand With Jensen” petition topping 180,200 signatures, backing from Elon Musk, and President Trump saying he would not mind seeing Huang reinstated; shares fell 4.12% Monday ahead of Tuesday’s earnings.

breaking.headline: California sues OpenAI over rogue AI agents
breaking.fact: California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI on Monday in San Francisco Superior Court, the first state suit over its AI agents carrying out cyberattacks — at least 80 incidents, including July’s hack of Hugging Face — accusing the company of testing dangerous models without adequate safeguards; he seeks an injunction, $2,500 per violation and disgorgement.

breaking.headline: Fed Chair Warsh maps three AI scenarios, gives no rate signal
breaking.fact: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh laid out three “super intelligence” scenarios Monday in San Francisco — growth running above trend, jobs displaced and unemployment higher, or AI returns disappointing and stocks falling — while giving no signal on rates and never mentioning inflation; December-hike odds stay above 90%, and Governor Barr flagged more than $3 trillion in off-balance-sheet AI financing.

weekInBrief.headline: Japan’s economy shrinks unexpectedly in Q3
weekInBrief.body: Japan’s economy unexpectedly shrank 0.1% in the third quarter, with higher energy prices cited as a factor, against forecasts for growth — a soft spot in the global picture as markets slide and trade frictions linger.

weekInBrief.headline: Ukraine launches its largest drone attack of the war
weekInBrief.body: Ukraine launched its biggest overnight drone attack on Russia since the war began, with Russia saying it downed 1,336 Ukrainian drones across 16 regions overnight, including around Moscow, as diplomatic efforts over the war remain under pressure heading into winter.

weekInBrief.headline: COP31 climate talks enter a decisive phase in Antalya
weekInBrief.body: Delegates at the COP31 climate talks in Antalya entered a decisive phase of negotiations over fossil fuels, climate finance and the pace of the global energy transition, with difficult talks still ahead before the summit closes.

weekInBrief.headline: Italy fines Meta $887 million over Facebook photo use
weekInBrief.body: Italy fined Meta $887 million for using photos and videos from Android users’ Facebook galleries without specific consent, the latest big European privacy penalty against a U.S. tech giant and a reminder that regulators keep tightening the screws on the ad model.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: Iran’s navy claimed a fourth tanker caught fire Monday after hitting a mine east of the strait, bringing its claimed total since Sunday to seven, and warned of “serious” repercussions for vessels sailing without its authorization; none of the claims has been independently verified. The U.S. naval buildup grew with the arrival of the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group on Sunday, bringing the regional deployment to three carrier strike groups and more than 20 surface combatants enforcing the blockade. On oil, the blockade still holds — Kpler’s Nov 10 briefing put total Hormuz clearance at 7.8 million barrels a day over the prior week, about 46% of pre-war, with Iranian-origin cargoes excluded throughout, and Kpler data cited in reporting put Iranian shipments at zero since Aug 25, while Gulf exports counted with pipeline and bypass volumes run near pre-war levels.

space.headline: Euclid space telescope discovers its first comet
space.body: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first comet, C/2026 S1 — “comet Euclid” — spotted about 807 million miles away in observations from Sept. 16–24. A fuzzy cloud around the object showed it shedding dust and gas; the find was a bonus for a mission built to study dark energy and dark matter, not fast-moving comets.

space.headline: Star’s repeated outbursts traced to a hidden companion
space.body: Astronomers have solved the mystery of AT 2016blu, a giant star that survived at least 27 violent outbursts since 2012: a hidden companion — a black hole or a neutron star — pulls gas from the star on every close pass, about every 113 days. Chandra X-ray data from March 2026 showed the star 100 times brighter in X-rays than in 2001–02; the study appears in The Astrophysical Journal.

space.headline: New tool tracks unintended CRISPR edits cell by cell
space.body: Salk scientists have built Superb-seq, a method that reads out all CRISPR edits — on- and off-target — and their effects on gene activity at single-cell resolution. In 10,000 human leukemia cells it detected 43 edit sites, 36 of them off-target; the study was published in Nature Methods on Nov. 16.

space.headline: Ultra-thin MXene materials point to faster energy storage
space.body: An international team has found that a chemical reaction triggered at a single tiny point on an ultra-thin MXene flake can spread across much of the material, revealing connectivity never seen before. Published in Nature Communications, the finding sheds new light on materials being explored for faster, more efficient energy storage and hydrogen technologies.

apod.title: A storm of new stars
apod.credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, D. Thilker, F. Belfiore, J. Lee and the PHANGS-HST Team — ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week
apod.explanation: NGC 1792 is a starburst galaxy over 50 million light-years away in the constellation Columba, its spiral arms rich in star-forming regions. Gravitational interaction with its larger neighbour NGC 1808 stirred its gas reserves into a torrent of star formation; the red H-alpha glow in its arms marks dense hydrogen clouds where new stars are being born.
